metadata.name: stg_workday_financial_management__business_plan_detail
metadata.comment: Each record represents the header of a business plan, which is how Workday stores budgets. One row per plan, per company, per fiscal period. The budgeted amounts live on stg_workday_financial_management__business_plan_entry_line.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

business_plan_detail_key.name: business_plan_detail_key
business_plan_detail_key.comment: Surrogate key derived from business_plan_detail_id, business_plan_detail_index, and source_relation.

business_plan_detail_id.name: business_plan_detail_id
business_plan_detail_id.comment:
Unique identifier of the business plan. Workday stores budgets as business plans, so this is the
budget equivalent of journal_entry_id.

business_plan_detail_index.name: business_plan_detail_index
business_plan_detail_index.comment:
Position of the plan within its parent record. The connector unpacks business plans from a nested
structure, and in observed data this is always 0. It is carried and joined on anyway, so a tenant
that does emit more than one stays correct.

business_plan_reference_id.name: business_plan_reference_id
business_plan_reference_id.comment: Business key of the plan, distinct from the surrogate identifier in business_plan_detail_id.

company_id.name: company_id
company_id.comment: Reference to the company the journal entry belongs to.

currency_id.name: currency_id
currency_id.comment: Reference to the currency the amounts are recorded in.

business_plan_structure_id.name: business_plan_structure_id
business_plan_structure_id.comment:
Reference to the business plan structure, which defines the plan's shape and rules. The connector
syncs no business plan structure table, so you cannot resolve this identifier to a name.

organizing_dimension_id.name: organizing_dimension_id
organizing_dimension_id.comment:
Reference to the dimension the plan is organized by. The connector syncs no table for this, so you
cannot resolve this identifier to a name.

plan_year.name: plan_year
plan_year.comment:
Fiscal year the plan covers, as an integer. Together with fiscal_time_interval_id this places the
plan on a fiscal period. A value of 0 means the plan carries no period at all and cannot be placed
on a timeline.

fiscal_time_interval_id.name: fiscal_time_interval_id
fiscal_time_interval_id.comment:
Reference to the posting interval within the fiscal year the plan budgets for. This is the same
identifier fiscal_period exposes as fiscal_posting_interval_id -- join on both this and the plan's
year, because an interval identifies a position in the year and repeats across years.

fiscal_posting_interval_code.name: fiscal_posting_interval_code
fiscal_posting_interval_code.comment: Code of the posting interval, for example the name of the month or quarter it represents.

award_posting_interval_code.name: award_posting_interval_code
award_posting_interval_code.comment:
Code of the award posting interval, used when the plan budgets against a grant award rather than a
fiscal schedule.

award_contract_id.name: award_contract_id
award_contract_id.comment: Reference to the award contract the plan budgets against, for grant accounting.

award_proposal_code.name: award_proposal_code
award_proposal_code.comment: Code of the award proposal the plan budgets against, for grant accounting.

project_budget_code.name: project_budget_code
project_budget_code.comment: Code of the project budget the plan belongs to, for project-based budgeting.

business_plan_memo.name: business_plan_memo
business_plan_memo.comment: Free-text memo entered on the business plan header.

_fivetran_synced.name: _fivetran_synced
_fivetran_synced.comment: Timestamp of when Fivetran last synced this row.

metadata.name: stg_workday_financial_management__business_plan_entry_line
metadata.comment: Each record represents a single budgeted amount on a business plan, and this is the grain budget is stored at. Workday records these as explicit debit and credit columns, the same way it records journal entry lines.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

business_plan_entry_line_id.name: business_plan_entry_line_id
business_plan_entry_line_id.comment: Surrogate key derived from business_plan_detail_id, business_plan_detail_index, business_plan_entry_line_index, and source_relation.

business_plan_detail_id.name: business_plan_detail_id
business_plan_detail_id.comment:
Unique identifier of the business plan. Workday stores budgets as business plans, so this is the
budget equivalent of journal_entry_id.

business_plan_detail_index.name: business_plan_detail_index
business_plan_detail_index.comment:
Position of the plan within its parent record. The connector unpacks business plans from a nested
structure, and in observed data this is always 0. It is carried and joined on anyway, so a tenant
that does emit more than one stays correct.

business_plan_entry_line_index.name: business_plan_entry_line_index
business_plan_entry_line_index.comment:
Position of the line within its business plan. Together with business_plan_detail_id and
business_plan_detail_index this forms the grain of the business plan entry line table, and it is
the key the budget worktag bridge joins on.

line_order.name: line_order
line_order.comment:
Display ordering token of the line within the plan. A string rather than a number, and not used as
a join key.

ledger_account_id.name: ledger_account_id
ledger_account_id.comment:
Reference to the ledger account the budgeted amount applies to. This resolves against
ledger_account, which is the same identifier space the journal line exposes as
ledger_account_code -- that is what lets budget and actuals pair on account.

ledger_account_summary_id.name: ledger_account_summary_id
ledger_account_summary_id.comment:
Reference to the ledger account summary the budgeted amount applies to, when a plan budgets at a
rollup level rather than an individual account.

debit_amount.name: debit_amount
debit_amount.comment: Budgeted debit amount on the line, in the plan's currency.

credit_amount.name: credit_amount
credit_amount.comment: Budgeted credit amount on the line, in the plan's currency.

business_plan_entry_line_memo.name: business_plan_entry_line_memo
business_plan_entry_line_memo.comment: Free-text memo entered on the business plan line.

business_plan_detail_id.name: business_plan_detail_id
business_plan_detail_id.comment:
Unique identifier of the business plan. Workday stores budgets as business plans, so this is the
budget equivalent of journal_entry_id.

business_plan_detail_index.name: business_plan_detail_index
business_plan_detail_index.comment:
Position of the plan within its parent record. The connector unpacks business plans from a nested
structure, and in observed data this is always 0. It is carried and joined on anyway, so a tenant

business_plan_entry_line_index.name: business_plan_entry_line_index
business_plan_entry_line_index.comment:
Position of the line within its business plan. Together with business_plan_detail_id and
business_plan_detail_index this forms the grain of the business plan entry line table, and it is
the key the budget worktag bridge joins on.

worktag_id.name: worktag_id

metadata.name: stg_workday_financial_management__company
metadata.comment: Each record represents a company, the legal entity that journal entries post to. This model also carries the accounting sign-convention settings that govern how debits and credits are stored.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

company_id.name: company_id
company_id.comment: Reference to the company the journal entry belongs to.

currency_id.name: currency_id
currency_id.comment: Reference to the currency the amounts are recorded in.

account_set_id.name: account_set_id
account_set_id.comment: Reference to the account set, the chart of accounts grouping the account belongs to.

is_active.name: is_active
is_active.comment: Whether the company is currently active.

fiscal_schedule_code.name: fiscal_schedule_code
fiscal_schedule_code.comment:
Code of the fiscal schedule the company reports on, for example Standard_Corporate_Schedule or
May_April. Join it to fiscal_year to resolve the schedule, and from there to fiscal_period for
period start and end dates.

default_reporting_book_code.name: default_reporting_book_code
default_reporting_book_code.comment: Code of the company's default reporting book.

is_debit_credit_reversed.name: is_debit_credit_reversed
is_debit_credit_reversed.comment:
Whether the company reverses the debit and credit convention. Affects how you derive signed
amounts from debit_amount and credit_amount.

is_sign_reversed.name: is_sign_reversed
is_sign_reversed.comment:
Whether the company keeps the debit and credit split but reverses the sign. Affects how you derive
signed amounts from debit_amount and credit_amount.

Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple

custom_worktag_id.name: custom_worktag_id
custom_worktag_id.comment: Unique identifier of the custom worktag.

configuration_code.comment:
Code of the tenant configuration that defines this custom worktag type. This is the custom worktag
equivalent of worktag_type, and is what you name in workday_financial_management__worktag_types to
give a custom worktag its own column on the general ledger.

metadata.name: stg_workday_financial_management__fiscal_period
metadata.comment: Each record represents one accounting period of a fiscal schedule, with its start and end dates. This is the period definition budgets are stored against. Note that a period is identified by schedule, year, and posting interval together, because a posting interval names a position in the year and repeats every year.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

fiscal_period_id.name: fiscal_period_id
fiscal_period_id.comment: Surrogate key derived from fiscal_schedule_id, fiscal_year_name, fiscal_posting_interval_id, and source_relation. The source carries no key of its own.

fiscal_schedule_id.name: fiscal_schedule_id
fiscal_schedule_id.comment:
Reference to the fiscal schedule the period or year belongs to. Resolve a company to its schedule
through the company's fiscal_schedule_code.

fiscal_year_name.name: fiscal_year_name
fiscal_year_name.comment: Name of the fiscal year, for example 2025. Part of the key that identifies a fiscal period.

fiscal_posting_interval_id.name: fiscal_posting_interval_id
fiscal_posting_interval_id.comment:
Reference to the posting interval, which is a position within the fiscal year rather than a
specific period. The same interval repeats every year, so a period is identified by schedule, year,
and interval together.

fiscal_posting_interval_code.name: fiscal_posting_interval_code
fiscal_posting_interval_code.comment: Code of the posting interval, for example the name of the month or quarter it represents.

fiscal_month_start_date.name: fiscal_month_start_date
fiscal_month_start_date.comment:
First day of the fiscal period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule this does not fall on the first day
of a calendar month.

fiscal_month_end_date.name: fiscal_month_end_date
fiscal_month_end_date.comment:
Last day of the fiscal period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule this does not fall on the last day of
a calendar month, and a single fiscal period can span two calendar months.

metadata.comment: Each record represents one fiscal year of a fiscal schedule, with its start and end dates. Resolves a company's fiscal_schedule_code to a schedule, and gives year-to-date figures the boundary they reset on.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

fiscal_year_id.name: fiscal_year_id
fiscal_year_id.comment: Unique identifier of the fiscal year.

fiscal_schedule_id.name: fiscal_schedule_id
fiscal_schedule_id.comment:
Reference to the fiscal schedule the period or year belongs to. Resolve a company to its schedule
through the company's fiscal_schedule_code.

fiscal_schedule_code.name: fiscal_schedule_code
fiscal_schedule_code.comment:
Code of the fiscal schedule the company reports on, for example Standard_Corporate_Schedule or
May_April. Join it to fiscal_year to resolve the schedule, and from there to fiscal_period for
period start and end dates.

fiscal_year_name.name: fiscal_year_name
fiscal_year_name.comment: Name of the fiscal year, for example 2025. Part of the key that identifies a fiscal period.

fiscal_year_number.name: fiscal_year_number
fiscal_year_number.comment: Numeric form of the fiscal year.

fiscal_year_start_date.name: fiscal_year_start_date
fiscal_year_start_date.comment:
First day of the fiscal year. This is the boundary year-to-date figures reset on, and it is not
January 1 for a company on a non-calendar schedule.

fiscal_year_end_date.name: fiscal_year_end_date
fiscal_year_end_date.comment: Last day of the fiscal year.

metadata.name: stg_workday_financial_management__journal_entry
metadata.comment: Each record represents the header of an accounting journal entry, carrying the accounting date, status, source system, ledger, and company the entry posts to. Debit and credit amounts live on stg_workday_financial_management__journal_entry_line.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

journal_entry_id.name: journal_entry_id
journal_entry_id.comment: Unique identifier of the journal entry.

company_id.name: company_id
company_id.comment: Reference to the company the journal entry belongs to.

ledger_id.name: ledger_id
ledger_id.comment: Reference to the ledger the journal entry posts to.

journal_source_id.name: journal_source_id
journal_source_id.comment: Reference to the source system or process that generated the entry.

currency_id.name: currency_id
currency_id.comment: Reference to the currency the amounts are recorded in.

ledger_period_id.name: ledger_period_id
ledger_period_id.comment:
Reference to the Workday ledger period. The connector does not sync a ledger period table, so you
cannot resolve this identifier to a period name or date range.

accounting_date.name: accounting_date
accounting_date.comment:
Date the entry posts to the ledger. Financial reporting periods derive from this date, not from
transaction_date.

transaction_date.name: transaction_date
transaction_date.comment: Date the underlying business transaction occurred.

created_at.name: created_at
created_at.comment: Timestamp the journal entry record was created in Workday.

journal_number.name: journal_number
journal_number.comment: Human-readable journal number assigned by Workday.

journal_sequence_number.name: journal_sequence_number
journal_sequence_number.comment: Sequence number of the journal entry within its ledger and period.

journal_entry_status.name: journal_entry_status
journal_entry_status.comment: Processing status of the entry, for example Posted, Draft, or Cancelled.

book_code.name: book_code
book_code.comment: Code of the accounting book the entry posts to.

journal_entry_memo.name: journal_entry_memo
journal_entry_memo.comment: Free-text memo entered on the journal header.

external_reference_id.name: external_reference_id
external_reference_id.comment: Identifier of the entry in the external system that originated it.

total_ledger_debits.name: total_ledger_debits
total_ledger_debits.comment: Control total of all debit amounts across the entry's lines, in ledger currency.

total_ledger_credits.name: total_ledger_credits
total_ledger_credits.comment: Control total of all credit amounts across the entry's lines, in ledger currency.

cancel_reverses_journal_entry_id.name: cancel_reverses_journal_entry_id
cancel_reverses_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that this entry cancels and reverses.

cancel_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.name: cancel_reversed_by_journal_entry_id
cancel_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that cancels and reverses this entry.

functional_reverses_journal_entry_id.name: functional_reverses_journal_entry_id
functional_reverses_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that this entry functionally reverses.

functional_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.name: functional_reversed_by_journal_entry_id
functional_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that functionally reverses this entry.

_fivetran_synced.name: _fivetran_synced
_fivetran_synced.comment: Timestamp of when Fivetran last synced this row.

has_stats.description: Indicates whether there are statistics for this table

metadata.name: stg_workday_financial_management__journal_entry_line
metadata.comment: Each record represents a single debit or credit line of a journal entry. This is the transactional grain of the general ledger. Workday stores debits and credits as explicit columns in both transaction and ledger currency.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

journal_entry_line_id.name: journal_entry_line_id
journal_entry_line_id.comment: Surrogate key derived from journal_entry_id, journal_entry_line_index, and source_relation.

journal_entry_id.name: journal_entry_id
journal_entry_id.comment: Unique identifier of the journal entry.

journal_entry_line_index.name: journal_entry_line_index
journal_entry_line_index.comment:
Position of the line within its parent journal entry. Together with journal_entry_id this forms
the grain of the journal entry line table, and it is the key the worktag bridge joins on.

line_order.name: line_order
line_order.comment:
Display ordering of the line within the entry. Distinct from journal_entry_line_index and not used
as a join key.

journal_line_number.name: journal_line_number
journal_line_number.comment: Line number assigned by Workday, visible to you on the journal.

ledger_account_id.name: ledger_account_id
ledger_account_id.comment: Reference to the ledger account the line posts to.

ledger_account_code.name: ledger_account_code
ledger_account_code.comment:
Code of the ledger account, denormalized onto the journal line. The ledger account table does not
carry this code, so the line is the only place it is available.

account_set_name.name: account_set_name
account_set_name.comment: Name of the account set the ledger account belongs to, denormalized onto the journal line.

line_company_id.name: line_company_id
line_company_id.comment:
Reference to the company the line posts to. May differ from the journal header's company on
intercompany entries.

currency_id.name: currency_id
currency_id.comment: Reference to the currency the amounts are recorded in.

debit_amount.name: debit_amount
debit_amount.comment: Debit amount on the line, in the transaction currency.

credit_amount.name: credit_amount
credit_amount.comment: Credit amount on the line, in the transaction currency.

ledger_debit_amount.name: ledger_debit_amount
ledger_debit_amount.comment: Debit amount on the line, converted to the ledger's functional currency.

ledger_credit_amount.name: ledger_credit_amount
ledger_credit_amount.comment: Credit amount on the line, converted to the ledger's functional currency.

currency_rate.name: currency_rate
currency_rate.comment: Exchange rate applied to convert the transaction currency amounts into ledger currency amounts.

quantity.name: quantity
quantity.comment: Statistical or unit quantity recorded on the line.

budget_date.name: budget_date
budget_date.comment: Date used to align the line against budget periods.

journal_entry_line_memo.name: journal_entry_line_memo
journal_entry_line_memo.comment: Free-text memo entered on the journal line.

exclude_from_spend_report.name: exclude_from_spend_report
exclude_from_spend_report.comment: Whether the line is excluded from Workday spend reporting.

metadata.name: workday_financial_management__budget_vs_actuals
metadata.comment:
Budget and actual activity paired on the dimensions they share, with variance and fiscal year-to-date figures. One row per company, ledger account, currency, and fiscal period, per source relation.
Workday stores budgets as business plans, and business plans are recorded against fiscal periods rather than calendar months. This model is therefore grained on fiscal periods, which is why its period columns are named fiscal_* and do not line up with the calendar months in workday_financial_management__general_ledger_by_period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule a fiscal period spans parts of two calendar months, so the two models are not joinable on period. Join them on company and ledger account only, or use the fiscal_* columns the general ledger carries at line grain.
Only periods where a budget or actual figure exists are emitted. Periods where an account has neither are left out rather than padded with zeroes.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

budget_vs_actuals_id.name: budget_vs_actuals_id
budget_vs_actuals_id.comment: Surrogate key derived from company_id, ledger_account_id, currency_id, fiscal_period_id, and source_relation.

company_id.name: company_id
company_id.comment: Reference to the company the journal entry belongs to.

company_name.name: company_name
company_name.comment:
Name of the company.
Null where the plan references a company that is missing from the source.

ledger_account_id.name: ledger_account_id
ledger_account_id.comment: Reference to the ledger account budget and actuals are paired on. This is the identifier the ledger account dimension is keyed by. Note that the general ledger exposes this same value as ledger_account_code, not as its own ledger_account_id, which is a separate identifier that resolves to nothing.

ledger_account_name.name: ledger_account_name
ledger_account_name.comment:
Name of the ledger account.
Null where the account code appears in more than one account set. See DECISIONLOG.

ledger_account_type.name: ledger_account_type
ledger_account_type.comment:
Type of the ledger account.
Null where the account code appears in more than one account set.

currency_id.name: currency_id
currency_id.comment: Identifier of the currency both figures on the row are stated in. Currency is part of the key, so budget and actuals recorded in different currencies stay as separate unpaired rows rather than producing a variance across currencies.

currency_code.name: currency_code
currency_code.comment: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example USD or EUR.

fiscal_schedule_code.name: fiscal_schedule_code
fiscal_schedule_code.comment:
Code of the fiscal schedule the company reports on, for example Standard_Corporate_Schedule or
May_April. Join it to fiscal_year to resolve the schedule, and from there to fiscal_period for
period start and end dates.

fiscal_year_name.name: fiscal_year_name
fiscal_year_name.comment:
Name of the fiscal year, for example 2025. Part of the key that identifies a fiscal period.
This is the boundary the year-to-date columns accumulate within.

fiscal_year_start_date.name: fiscal_year_start_date
fiscal_year_start_date.comment:
First day of the fiscal year. This is the boundary year-to-date figures reset on, and it is not
January 1 for a company on a non-calendar schedule.

fiscal_year_end_date.name: fiscal_year_end_date
fiscal_year_end_date.comment: Last day of the fiscal year.

fiscal_period_id.name: fiscal_period_id
fiscal_period_id.comment: Identifier of the fiscal period this row reports on.

fiscal_month_name.name: fiscal_month_name
fiscal_month_name.comment: Code of the posting interval, for example the name of the month or quarter it represents.

fiscal_month_start_date.name: fiscal_month_start_date
fiscal_month_start_date.comment:
First day of the fiscal period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule this does not fall on the first day
of a calendar month.

fiscal_month_end_date.name: fiscal_month_end_date
fiscal_month_end_date.comment:
Last day of the fiscal period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule this does not fall on the last day of
a calendar month, and a single fiscal period can span two calendar months.

has_budget.name: has_budget
has_budget.comment: Whether a budget figure exists for this combination. Distinguishes a budget of zero from no budget at all, which budget_amount alone cannot.

has_actuals.name: has_actuals
has_actuals.comment: Whether actual activity exists for this combination. False on a budgeted account that saw no posting in the period.

budget_amount.name: budget_amount
budget_amount.comment: Budgeted movement for the period, calculated as budgeted debits minus credits. Positive is a debit, matching the general ledger's net_amount convention. Zero where no budget exists, so read has_budget alongside it.

actual_amount.name: actual_amount
actual_amount.comment: Actual movement for the period, the sum of the general ledger's ledger_net_amount for the lines whose accounting date falls in this fiscal period. Zero where no activity exists.

variance_amount.name: variance_amount
variance_amount.comment: actual_amount minus budget_amount. Whether a positive number is favourable depends on the account: on an expense account it means overspend, on a revenue account it means outperformance.

variance_percent.name: variance_percent
variance_percent.comment: variance_amount as a proportion of the budget's magnitude. Null where budget_amount is zero, since there is no baseline to compare against.

budget_amount_year_to_date.name: budget_amount_year_to_date
budget_amount_year_to_date.comment: Running total of budget_amount within the fiscal year, through the end of this period.

actual_amount_year_to_date.name: actual_amount_year_to_date
actual_amount_year_to_date.comment: Running total of actual_amount within the fiscal year, through the end of this period.

has_stats.label: Has Stats?
has_stats.description: Indicates whether there are statistics for this table

metadata.name: workday_financial_management__general_ledger
metadata.comment:
Transaction-level general ledger detail. One row per journal entry line, per source relation. Journal header, company, ledger, ledger account, journal source, and currency context are denormalized onto every line. Only posted journal entries are included.
Workday supplies debits and credits natively, so both the debit/credit pair and a signed net_amount are exposed. Note that negative debit and credit amounts are legitimate: a company configured for "Keep Debit/Credit and Reverse Sign" records its reversals as a negative amount in the original column rather than moving it to the opposite column.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

general_ledger_id.comment: Surrogate key derived from journal_entry_id, journal_entry_line_index, and source_relation.

journal_entry_id.name: journal_entry_id
journal_entry_id.comment: Unique identifier of the journal entry.

journal_entry_line_index.name: journal_entry_line_index
journal_entry_line_index.comment:
Position of the line within its parent journal entry. Together with journal_entry_id this forms
the grain of the journal entry line table, and it is the key the worktag bridge joins on.

journal_number.name: journal_number
journal_number.comment: Human-readable journal number assigned by Workday.

journal_sequence_number.name: journal_sequence_number
journal_sequence_number.comment: Sequence number of the journal entry within its ledger and period.

journal_entry_status.name: journal_entry_status
journal_entry_status.comment: Processing status of the entry, for example Posted, Draft, or Cancelled.

book_code.name: book_code
book_code.comment: Code of the accounting book the entry posts to.

accounting_date.name: accounting_date
accounting_date.comment:
Date the entry posts to the ledger. Financial reporting periods derive from this date, not from
transaction_date.

transaction_date.name: transaction_date
transaction_date.comment: Date the underlying business transaction occurred.

created_at.name: created_at
created_at.comment: Timestamp the journal entry record was created in Workday.

budget_date.name: budget_date
budget_date.comment: Date used to align the line against budget periods.

fiscal_schedule_code.name: fiscal_schedule_code
fiscal_schedule_code.comment:
Code of the fiscal schedule the company reports on, for example Standard_Corporate_Schedule or
May_April. Join it to fiscal_year to resolve the schedule, and from there to fiscal_period for
period start and end dates.
Present only when workday_financial_management_using_fiscal_calendar is enabled.

fiscal_year_name.name: fiscal_year_name
fiscal_year_name.comment: Fiscal year the line's accounting date falls in, on the schedule its company reports on. This is not the calendar year for a company on a non-calendar schedule.

fiscal_year_start_date.name: fiscal_year_start_date
fiscal_year_start_date.comment:
First day of the fiscal year. This is the boundary year-to-date figures reset on, and it is not
January 1 for a company on a non-calendar schedule.

fiscal_year_end_date.name: fiscal_year_end_date
fiscal_year_end_date.comment: Last day of the fiscal year.

fiscal_period_id.name: fiscal_period_id
fiscal_period_id.comment: Identifier of the fiscal period the line's accounting date falls in. A line has one accounting date, so it lands in exactly one period.

fiscal_month_name.name: fiscal_month_name
fiscal_month_name.comment: Code of the posting interval, for example the name of the month or quarter it represents.

fiscal_month_start_date.name: fiscal_month_start_date
fiscal_month_start_date.comment:
First day of the fiscal period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule this does not fall on the first day
of a calendar month.

fiscal_month_end_date.name: fiscal_month_end_date
fiscal_month_end_date.comment:
Last day of the fiscal period. On a 4-4-5 or similar schedule this does not fall on the last day of
a calendar month, and a single fiscal period can span two calendar months.

company_id.name: company_id
company_id.comment: Reference to the company the journal entry belongs to.

line_company_id.name: line_company_id
line_company_id.comment:
Reference to the company the line posts to. May differ from the journal header's company on
intercompany entries.

ledger_id.name: ledger_id
ledger_id.comment: Reference to the ledger the journal entry posts to.

ledger_type.name: ledger_type
ledger_type.comment: Type of ledger, for example Actuals, Budget, or Commitment.

ledger_account_id.name: ledger_account_id
ledger_account_id.comment: Reference to the ledger account the line posts to.

ledger_account_code.name: ledger_account_code
ledger_account_code.comment:
Code of the ledger account, denormalized onto the journal line. The ledger account table does not
carry this code, so the line is the only place it is available.

ledger_account_name.name: ledger_account_name
ledger_account_name.comment:
Name of the ledger account.
Null where the account code appears in more than one account set. See DECISIONLOG.

ledger_account_type.name: ledger_account_type
ledger_account_type.comment:
Type of the ledger account.
Null where the account code appears in more than one account set. See DECISIONLOG.

account_set_id.name: account_set_id
account_set_id.comment:
Reference to the account set, the chart of accounts grouping the account belongs to.
Null where the account code appears in more than one account set. See DECISIONLOG.

account_set_name.name: account_set_name
account_set_name.comment: Name of the account set the ledger account belongs to, denormalized onto the journal line.

journal_source_id.name: journal_source_id
journal_source_id.comment: Reference to the source system or process that generated the entry.

journal_source_name.name: journal_source_name
journal_source_name.comment: Name of the journal source, for example Manual Journal, Supplier Invoice, or Payroll.

currency_id.name: currency_id
currency_id.comment: Reference to the currency the amounts are recorded in.

currency_code.name: currency_code
currency_code.comment: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example USD or EUR.

ledger_currency_id.name: ledger_currency_id
ledger_currency_id.comment: Identifier of the ledger (functional) currency the ledger_* amount columns are stated in. Null where the ledger is missing from the source.

ledger_currency_code.name: ledger_currency_code
ledger_currency_code.comment: ISO code of the ledger (functional) currency. Unit for ledger_debit_amount, ledger_credit_amount, and ledger_net_amount. Null where the ledger is missing from the source.

currency_rate.name: currency_rate
currency_rate.comment: Exchange rate applied to convert the transaction currency amounts into ledger currency amounts.

debit_amount.name: debit_amount
debit_amount.comment: Debit amount on the line, in the transaction currency.

credit_amount.name: credit_amount
credit_amount.comment: Credit amount on the line, in the transaction currency.

net_amount.name: net_amount
net_amount.comment: Signed movement on the line in transaction currency, calculated as debit_amount minus credit_amount. Positive is a debit. Sum this instead of handling the debit and credit columns separately.

ledger_debit_amount.name: ledger_debit_amount
ledger_debit_amount.comment: Debit amount on the line, converted to the ledger's functional currency.

ledger_credit_amount.name: ledger_credit_amount
ledger_credit_amount.comment: Credit amount on the line, converted to the ledger's functional currency.

ledger_net_amount.name: ledger_net_amount
ledger_net_amount.comment: Signed movement on the line in the ledger's functional currency, calculated as ledger_debit_amount minus ledger_credit_amount. Positive is a debit.

quantity.name: quantity
quantity.comment: Statistical or unit quantity recorded on the line.

journal_line_number.name: journal_line_number
journal_line_number.comment: Line number assigned by Workday, visible to you on the journal.

line_order.name: line_order
line_order.comment:
Display ordering of the line within the entry. Distinct from journal_entry_line_index and not used
as a join key.

journal_entry_memo.name: journal_entry_memo
journal_entry_memo.comment: Free-text memo entered on the journal header.

journal_entry_line_memo.name: journal_entry_line_memo
journal_entry_line_memo.comment: Free-text memo entered on the journal line.

external_reference_id.name: external_reference_id
external_reference_id.comment: Identifier of the entry in the external system that originated it.

exclude_from_spend_report.name: exclude_from_spend_report
exclude_from_spend_report.comment: Whether the line is excluded from Workday spend reporting.

cancel_reverses_journal_entry_id.name: cancel_reverses_journal_entry_id
cancel_reverses_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that this entry cancels and reverses.

cancel_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.name: cancel_reversed_by_journal_entry_id
cancel_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that cancels and reverses this entry.

functional_reverses_journal_entry_id.name: functional_reverses_journal_entry_id
functional_reverses_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that this entry functionally reverses.

functional_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.name: functional_reversed_by_journal_entry_id
functional_reversed_by_journal_entry_id.comment: Reference to the journal entry that functionally reverses this entry.

is_debit_credit_reversed.name: is_debit_credit_reversed
is_debit_credit_reversed.comment:
Whether the company reverses the debit and credit convention. Affects how you derive signed
amounts from debit_amount and credit_amount.

is_sign_reversed.name: is_sign_reversed
is_sign_reversed.comment:
Whether the company keeps the debit and credit split but reverses the sign. Affects how you derive
signed amounts from debit_amount and credit_amount.

has_stats.description: Indicates whether there are statistics for this table

metadata.name: workday_financial_management__general_ledger_by_period
metadata.comment: Monthly general ledger rollup. One row per company, ledger account, ledger currency, and calendar month, per source relation. Months with no journal activity are still present, carrying the last known balance forward.

source_relation.name: source_relation
source_relation.comment:
Name of the schema or connection this record came from. Populated only when you union multiple
Workday Financial Management connections together with the workday_financial_management_sources
variable. Otherwise it is an empty string.

general_ledger_by_period_id.comment: Surrogate key derived from company_id, ledger_account_id, ledger_currency_id, period_first_day, and source_relation.

company_id.name: company_id
company_id.comment: Reference to the company the journal entry belongs to.

ledger_account_id.name: ledger_account_id
ledger_account_id.comment: Reference to the ledger account the line posts to.

ledger_account_type.name: ledger_account_type
ledger_account_type.comment:
Type of the ledger account.
Null where the account code appears in more than one account set.

ledger_currency_id.name: ledger_currency_id
ledger_currency_id.comment: Identifier of the ledger (functional) currency every amount in this model is stated in. Read from the company that owns the ledger. Null where the ledger is missing from the source.

ledger_currency_code.name: ledger_currency_code
ledger_currency_code.comment: ISO code of the ledger (functional) currency, and the unit for period_net_change, period_beginning_balance, and period_ending_balance. Null where the ledger is missing from the source, in which case those rows group together.

date_year.name: date_year
date_year.comment: First day of the calendar year the period falls in.

period_first_day.name: period_first_day
period_first_day.comment: First day of the calendar month this row reports on.

period_last_day.name: period_last_day
period_last_day.comment: Last day of the calendar month this row reports on.

period_net_change.name: period_net_change
period_net_change.comment: Net movement on the account within the period, the sum of the general ledger's ledger_net_amount. Zero in months with no activity.

period_beginning_balance.name: period_beginning_balance
period_beginning_balance.comment: Cumulative balance at the start of the period, carried forward from the last month with activity.

period_ending_balance.name: period_ending_balance
period_ending_balance.comment: Cumulative balance at the end of the period, carried forward across months with no activity.
